question: Should OpenClaw permanently support automatic Discord source-message subagent progress, and if so should it use this Discord-specific lifecycle/config surface or a narrower generic lifecycle and status-ownership contract?
rationale: The patch proves the behavior works, but code review cannot choose a new public configuration and plugin lifecycle boundary on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Sponsor a narrower generic contract
options.body: Keep the user-visible feature while consolidating terminal lifecycle delivery and reaction ownership behind a generic channel/status seam before reopening or replacing this PR.

options.title: Accept the proposed API
options.body: Reopen and land the feature after rebase while explicitly owning the seven settings, delivery-context field, and channel lifecycle callback as supported contracts.

options.title: Decline automatic progress
options.body: Leave automatic source-message progress out of core and rely on existing manual task/status and ordinary Discord progress surfaces.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrower generic contract
recommendation.body: Keep the user-visible feature while consolidating terminal lifecycle delivery and reaction ownership behind a generic channel/status seam before reopening or replacing this PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to cross-channel task visibility and Discord product surfaces.
